principle: Every autonomous proposition should preferably be born with a falsification path: 'What observation would make this idea less believable?'

null_competing_explanation.purpose: Primary competing scientific account if proposition false
null_competing_explanation.example: Dispersion effect is liquidity artifact — disappears when controlling spread quintile

disconfirming_observation_spec.purpose: Explicit answer to falsification birthright question

structure.description: Plain language: what would weaken belief

example.description: If high-dispersion names do not outperform low-dispersion within same liquidity tier over 5d
example.operational_test: Spread-adjusted quintile spread of forward returns <= 0

birth_certificate_link.pass_requires: Both fields populated with operational content

epistemic_status_interaction.after_FALSIFY: FALSIFIED — proposition inactive for execution queue
epistemic_status_interaction.WITHHELD: Surprise insufficient for strong claim — may still seek counterexample

design_intent.opr_exports: disconfirming_observation_spec as structured input to challenger adapter
design_intent.separation: OPR owns the falsification spec at birth; Challenger owns counterexperiment design later

future_challenger_connection.anti_leakage: Challenger must not use hidden benchmark phenomena to craft disconfirming tests during BB-Prop-01

evaluator_checks.reject_if: Only generic 'null is no effect' without operational threshold
